description: A mini-IDE for Pluto and Lua in VS Code: syntax highlighting, completion, hover, typing helpers, diagnostics, a Lua syntax check and a settings panel.

command.run.title: Plua: Run Script
command.lint.title: Plua: Lint Script
command.reindex.title: Plua: Rebuild Workspace Index

plua.language.markdownDescription: Language of the messages of the extension: labels in hovers and completion, diagnostics, status and output texts. `auto` follows the display language of the editor (Russian for Russian, English otherwise). It changes on the fly. The names and descriptions of settings and commands follow the display language of VS Code itself (command *Configure Display Language*).
plua.language.enumDescriptions.0: Follow the display language of the editor: Russian if it is Russian, English otherwise.
plua.lua.enable.markdownDescription: Enable language features (completion, hover, go-to-definition, signature help, outline, and diagnostics) for `.lua` files. Turn this off if another extension, such as `sumneko.lua`, already provides them, to avoid duplicate suggestions. Pluto files still see the declarations of Lua files they use while `#plua.lua.indexFiles#` is on.
plua.lua.indexFiles.markdownDescription: Read `.lua` files of the workspace into the index, so that Pluto code can complete, hover and navigate into the Lua modules it `require`s. Independent of `#plua.lua.enable#`: with that off, Lua files are only read, never decorated with features of their own.
plua.index.enabled.description: Index all Pluto files of the workspace to provide completion, hover and navigation across files. When disabled, only open files are analyzed.
plua.index.includeLua.markdownDescriptio: Also index `.lua` files, so that Lua modules used from Pluto code are known.
plua.index.includeLua.markdownDeprecatio: Use `#plua.lua.indexFiles#` instead. When disabled here, `.lua` files are still left out of the index.
plua.index.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of files and folders to leave out of the index.
plua.index.exclude.markdownDeprecationMe: Use `#plua.workspace.exclude#` instead. Patterns set here are still applied.
plua.workspace.useGitignore.markdownDesc: Leave files matched by the `.gitignore` in the root of the workspace folder out of the index. When disabled, `.gitignore` is not read even if it is listed in `#plua.workspace.ignoreFiles#`.
plua.workspace.exclude.markdownDescripti: Glob patterns of files and folders to leave out of the index, relative to the workspace folder, e.g. `**/vendor/**` or `build/**`. `files.exclude` always applies; `node_modules`, `.git` and `.vs` are always excluded.
plua.workspace.useSearchExclude.markdown: Also leave out files matched by `#search.exclude#`.
plua.index.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to index per workspace.
plua.completion.documentWords.descriptio: Suggest other words of the current document.
plua.completion.autoTriggerTypes.markdow: Open the list of types by itself when typing a type hint in a Pluto file: after `:` in `function f(a: `, `function f(): ` and `local x: `. Method calls such as `obj:method` are not affected. The list offers built-in types and the classes of the workspace, each also as nullable (`int?`).
plua.outline.showFunctionBody.markdownDe: Show the contents of functions in the Outline and breadcrumbs: local variables, nested functions and callbacks (and calls, see `#plua.outline.calls#`). When disabled, only classes, methods and function signatures are shown.
plua.outline.maxFileLines.markdownDescri: In files with more lines than this, the contents of functions are left out of the Outline to keep the editor responsive, as if `#plua.outline.showFunctionBody#` was disabled. `0` means no limit.
plua.outline.calls.markdownDescription: List the calls and `return` statements inside of functions in the Outline, to see what a function does without opening it. At most 50 per function. Requires `#plua.outline.showFunctionBody#`.
plua.outline.calls.enumDescriptions.1: List calls that are statements of their own, e.g. `util.toast(...)`, and `return` statements.
plua.outline.calls.enumDescriptions.2: Also list calls inside of expressions, e.g. `ENTITY.GET_ENTITY_COORDS(...)` in `local coords = v3.new(ENTITY.GET_ENTITY_COORDS(entity))`. Each called function is listed once per function.
plua.outline.localVariables.description: Show local variables declared inside functions and blocks in the Outline and breadcrumbs. File-level variables are always shown.
plua.outline.loopVariables.markdownDescr: Show loop variables (`for i = ...`, `for k, v in ...`) in the Outline.
plua.outline.parameters.description: Show function parameters as children of their function in the Outline.
plua.outline.anonymousFunctions.markdown: Show anonymous functions and block lambdas, e.g. `scheduler:add() callback`, in the Outline.
plua.outline.fields.markdownDescription: Show fields assigned via `self.name = ...` as members of their class in the Outline.
plua.outline.showValues.markdownDescript: Show the initial value of variables and fields next to their name in the Outline, e.g. `count = 0`.
plua.hover.sourcePath.markdownDescriptio: How hovers and completion details link to a declaration in another file. Declarations in the current file always show just `Line N`.
plua.hover.sourcePath.enumDescriptions.0: File name and line, e.g. `VehicleManager.pluto:75`. The full path is shown when pointing at the link.
plua.hover.sourcePath.enumDescriptions.1: Path relative to the workspace and line, e.g. `src/lib/game/VehicleManager.pluto:75`.
plua.hover.sourcePath.enumDescriptions.2: Don't show where a declaration comes from.
plua.hover.showFunctionBody.description: Show the source code of a function or method below its signature in hovers: comments removed, indentation normalized and logical blocks separated by blank lines.
plua.hover.maxBodyLines.markdownDescript: Longest function source shown in hovers, in lines; longer functions are cut with a `-- ... (+N lines)` note. `0` means no limit. Requires `#plua.hover.showFunctionBody#`.
plua.hover.maxDeclarations.description: Number of declarations shown in a hover when several declarations share a name. A link below them opens the list of all.
plua.highlight.applyColors.markdownDescr: Apply the colors of `plua.highlight.colors` and `plua.highlight.tableBracketColors` to Pluto files. The extension keeps them in `editor.tokenColorCustomizations` as rules named `Pluto: ...` and does not touch your other rules; turning this off removes them. Off by default, so the colors of your theme are used.
plua.highlight.colors.functionName: Names of declared functions and methods.
plua.highlight.colors.functionKeyword: The `function` keyword and the `->` of lambdas.
plua.highlight.colors.typeColon: The `:` before a type in a type hint.
plua.highlight.colors.markdownDescriptio: Color and style of each kind of token. Write `{ "color": "#FF8800", "fontStyle": "bold" }` (the color gets a color picker in `settings.json`) or the short form `"#FF8800 bold"`. Styles: `bold`, `italic`, `underline`. Takes effect when `plua.highlight.applyColors` is on.
plua.highlight.colors.returnType: The return type of a function: `void` in `function f(): void`, `bool?` in `function f(): bool?`.
plua.highlight.style.fontStyle: Font style: normal, bold, italic, underline or a combination.
plua.highlight.tableBracketColors.markdo: Colors of the braces `{ }` of tables by nesting depth: the first entry is for the outermost table, the next for the one inside, and so on; the list repeats when it is shorter than the depth (up to 8 levels are told apart). Each entry is written like in `plua.highlight.colors`, e.g. `[{ "color": "#E6B450" }, { "color": "#59C2FF", "fontStyle": "bold" }]`. Empty by default.
plua.highlight.style.color: Color for every theme, e.g. `#FF8800`. Click the swatch to pick one. `darkColor` / `lightColor` override it for dark / light themes.
plua.highlight.style.darkColor: Color for dark and high contrast themes. Falls back to `color`.
plua.highlight.style.lightColor: Color for light themes (and high contrast light). Falls back to `color`.
plua.compilers.list.markdownDescription: Interpreters and compilers started to check code without running it. Each entry has a `language` (`pluto` or `lua`) and a `path` (a full path or a command name from the `PATH`; `${userHome}` and `${env:NAME}` work). For each language the first entry that exists is used; if none does, `#plua.diagnostics.compilerPath#` / `#plua.lua.compilerPath#` and then automatic detection apply. Machine-level setting: a workspace cannot choose which program is started.
plua.lua.checkSyntax.markdownDescription: Check `.lua` files for syntax errors with a Lua interpreter while `plua.lua.enable` is on. The interpreter is `plua.lua.compilerPath`, else `luac`, `lua` or `luajit` found in `bin/lua`, `tools/lua` and similar folders of the workspace, else on the `PATH`. The code is only compiled, never run. Without an interpreter only the built-in checks work.
plua.lua.compilerPath.markdownDescriptio: Path to `luac` / `lua` / `luajit` used to check `.lua` files. Supports `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}` and `${env:NAME}`. When empty, the workspace is searched (`bin/lua/luac.exe`, `tools/lua/lua.exe`, ...; the newest version wins), then the `PATH`.
plua.json.enable.markdownDescription: Check the paths of files written in JSON files (`"entry": "src/main.pluto"`): a path whose file does not exist gets a warning, with a quick fix when the file was moved. Which JSON files are checked is set by `plua.json.files`.
plua.json.files.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of the JSON files whose paths are checked, relative to the workspace folder, e.g. `**/info.json`, `config/*.json`, `**/*.json`. The `id`, `entry` and `dependencies` of a module manifest (`info.json`) are always checked.
plua.json.extensions.markdownDescription: Extensions of the files whose paths are checked in the JSON files above. A string is taken for a path only when it ends with one of them (and is not a URL or a pattern).
plua.json.checkAllPaths.markdownDescript: Check the paths of files with any extension that exists in the project folder (`.png`, `.txt`, ...), not only those of `plua.json.extensions`. Needs an open folder: its file names are read once, without the files excluded by `.gitignore`, `.plutoignore`, `.luaignore` and `files.exclude`.
plua.json.severity.markdownDescription: How a missing file is shown: `warning` (default), `error` or `information`.
plua.json.notifyNoFolder.markdownDescrip: Tell once per window that without an open folder the paths in a JSON file are checked only next to it.
plua.workspace.ignoreFiles.markdownDescr: Ignore files (`.gitignore` syntax) in the workspace root to read exclusions from: by default `.gitignore`, `.plutoignore` and `.luaignore`. Excluded files are not indexed, so they get no completion or go to definition.
plua.format.multilineParams.markdownDesc: Smart formatting of the parameter list of a function declaration whose `)` is on a line of its own (`.pluto` and `.lua` files): the first parameter typed right after `(` moves to the next line, one level deeper, and Enter at the end of a parameter adds the missing comma and starts the next line with the same indentation. One-line lists are left alone.
plua.format.multilineTables.markdownDesc: Smart formatting of a table whose `}` is on a line of its own (`.pluto` and `.lua` files): the first field typed right after `{` moves to the next line, one level deeper, and Enter at the end of a field adds the missing comma (before a `-- comment`) and starts the next line with the same indentation. One-line tables, and statements inside functions in a table, are left alone.
plua.highlight.paramNoDefault.markdownDe: Underline in yellow the type of the parameter of a function declaration the cursor is on when it has a type but no default value (`function f(test: bool)`). The line goes away when the cursor leaves the parameter or a comma is typed; a tooltip names the values that fit. Pluto files only.
plua.highlight.paramNoDefaultColor.markd: Color of that line in dark and high contrast themes. Any CSS color, e.g. `#E5C07B`.
Color of that line in light themes.
plua.completion.defaultValues.markdownDe: Suggest the values that can be given to a parameter as its default (`= false`, `= true` for `bool`, `= 0` for `int`, `= nil` for a nullable type, ...) when the cursor is right after its type: `function f(test: bool|)`. Pluto files only.
plua.completion.defaultValuesDelayMs.mar: Milliseconds the cursor has to rest right after the type of a parameter without a default value before the list of values opens by itself. `0` switches this off; the list can still be opened with `Ctrl+Space`.
plua.format.newLineAfterComma.markdownDe: After a comma typed at the end of an element of a multi-line parameter list or table, start a new line with the indentation of the elements, unless you go on typing (`test: bool = false, test1`) within `plua.format.newLineAfterCommaDelayMs`. `.pluto` and `.lua` files.
plua.format.newLineAfterCommaDelayMs.mar: Milliseconds to wait after the comma before the new line starts; typing or moving the cursor cancels it. `0` starts the line at once.
plua.format.suggestParens.markdownDescri: Show `()` in grey after `function` (also `function name`, `local f = function`); `Tab` inserts it and puts the cursor between the brackets. Nothing is shown when the brackets are already there. If inline suggestions are off (`editor.inlineSuggest.enabled`) it is not shown.
plua.format.suggestTableKeyAssign.markdo: Show ` = ` in grey after the key `["name"]` at the start of a field of a table; `Tab` inserts it.
plua.format.suggestBlockWords.markdownDe: Show ` then` in grey after the header of an `if` / `elseif`, and ` do` after the header of a `while` / `for`; `Tab` inserts it. Enter then adds the `end`.
plua.format.fixMismatchedBrackets.markdo: A closing bracket that does not fit the last opened one (`{ ]`) and matches no other open bracket: `off` ignores it, `suggest` underlines it and offers a quick fix (`Ctrl+.`), `auto` also replaces it by itself when you stop typing for `plua.format.fixMismatchedBracketsDelayMs`.
plua.format.fixMismatchedBrackets.sugges: Underline it and offer a quick fix.
plua.format.fixMismatchedBrackets.auto: Also replace it by itself after a pause.
plua.format.fixMismatchedBracketsDelayMs: Milliseconds to wait before `auto` replaces the closing bracket; typing or moving the cursor cancels it. `0` replaces it at once.
plua.diagnostics.duplicateParams.markdow: Report a name written twice in the parameters of a function or lambda (`function f(a, a)`) and a key written twice in a table (`{ a = 1, a = 2 }`): `warning` (default), `error` or `off`.
plua.format.ifBlockWord.markdownDescript: Which word is suggested after the header of an `if` / `elseif`: Pluto accepts both `if x then` and `if x do`. `auto` follows what the current file uses (and, if it uses both equally, the rest of the workspace; `then` when there is nothing to go by). Needs `plua.format.suggestBlockWords`.
plua.format.ifBlockWord.auto: Follow what the file and the workspace use.
plua.format.suggestFor.markdownDescripti: Suggestions while the header of a `for` is written, taken with `Tab` (`Alt+]` shows the next one): the kinds of loop after `for`, `pairs(...)` / `ipairs(...)` / `next, ...` after `in`, the limit `#table` of a numeric loop and its step. The ones that fit the nearest table of the file come first. ` do` after a finished header is `plua.format.suggestBlockWords`.
plua.format.nameStyle.markdownDescriptio: The words used for the variables in those suggestions: `short` (`i`, `k`, `v`, `t`) or `full` (`index`, `key`, `value`, `table_name`). The ready-made snippets are not affected.
plua.format.names.markdownDescription: Your own words for `index`, `key`, `value` and `table` in those suggestions, whichever style is chosen, e.g. `{ "value": "item", "table": "list" }`. Anything that is not a name, or is a reserved word, is ignored.
plua.hover.forPreview.markdownDescriptio: Hovering the `for` of a numeric loop with numbers (`for i = 1, 10, 2`) shows the values the variable goes through (1, 3, 5, 7, 9), and tells when the loop does not run.
plua.format.suggestParamType.markdownDes: Show a grey `:` after the name of a parameter that has no type (`function f(value2|)`) once the cursor has rested for `plua.format.suggestParamTypeDelayMs`, but not while the list of completions is open: it comes when that list is closed. `Tab` inserts `: ` and opens the list of types.
plua.format.suggestParamTypeDelayMs.mark: Milliseconds the cursor has to rest before the grey `:` of a parameter or of a return type (after the `)` of a function) is shown (the colon of a `case` comes at once). `0` shows it at once.
plua.format.suggestReturnType.markdownDe: Show a grey `: ` after the `)` of a function declaration that has no return type, after the same pause; `Tab` inserts it and opens the list of types.
plua.format.suggestReturnValue.markdownD: After `return ` in a function with a return type (`function f(): bool`), suggest the values that fit it (`true`, `false`; `0`, `1`, `nil`, ... by the type).
plua.format.suggestCaseColon.markdownDes: Show a grey `:` after the values of a `case` that has none (`case 1|`) at once, like the `()` after `function`; `Tab` inserts it.
plua.format.suggestCaseBreak.markdownDes: Show a grey `break` on an empty line in the body of a `case` that nothing ends yet (not `default`); `Tab` inserts it.
plua.format.suggestCaseWords.markdownDes: Show a grey `case ` and `default:` on an empty line at the level of the cases of a `switch`; `Tab` inserts it.
plua.highlight.paramNoType.markdownDescr: Underline in yellow the name of the parameter of a function declaration that has no type while the cursor is on it. The line goes away when the cursor leaves or a `:` is typed. The colors are those of `plua.highlight.paramNoDefaultColor`.
plua.highlight.caseNoColon.markdownDescr: Underline in yellow the word `case` of a `case` that has no `:` after its values while the cursor is on its line.
plua.diagnostics.returnTypes.markdownDes: Report a function that says it returns a type but never uses `return` (a nullable type, `void` and `any` are left alone), and a `void` function that returns a value: `warning` (default), `error` or `off`.
plua.diagnostics.caseFallthrough.markdow: Mark a `case` whose body is not ended by `break`, `return`, `goto` or `continue` and runs into the next `case` (`hint`). A case with an empty body, which gives two cases one body, is left alone. `off` by default: the Pluto compiler warns about it too.
plua.format.suggestConstructor.markdownD: In the body of a class that has no `__construct`, show a grey `function __construct()` on an empty line (and ` __construct()` after the word `function`); `Tab` inserts it with the cursor between the brackets. For a class that `extends` another one, `Alt+]` offers a second one that also calls `parent:__construct()`.
plua.highlight.nullableTypes.markdownDes: Highlight nullable types (`int?`, `?string`, `Vehicle?`) in type hints of Pluto files.
plua.highlight.nullableTypeColor.markdow: Color of nullable types in dark and high contrast themes. Any CSS color, e.g. `#FFFFFF`.
plua.highlight.nullableTypeLightColor.ma: Color of nullable types in light themes, where white would be invisible.
plua.autoCloseBlocks.markdownDescription: Insert the matching `end` (or `until`) when pressing Enter after a block opener such as `function`, `if ... then`, `for ... do`, `class` or `switch ... do`.
plua.quickDeleteEnd.markdownDescription: Press Backspace or Delete twice in a row on a line that holds only `end` (for example the one added by `plua.autoCloseBlocks`): the first press deletes a letter as usual, the second one, right after it, removes the whole line and puts the cursor at the end of the line above.
plua.quickDeleteEndDoubleMs.markdownDesc: How long (in milliseconds) after the first press of Backspace or Delete on a line with only `end` the second press still removes the line (see `plua.quickDeleteEnd`).
plua.shiftBackspaceDeleteFromBelow.enabl: Shift + Backspace deletes code from below, one token per press, without touching the indentation while a line has code: the last word or character of the line below the cursor, then that line itself once only spaces and tabs are left. Code to the right of the cursor goes first.
plua.shiftDeleteFromNextLine.markdownDes: Shift + Delete on an empty line (blank, or with indentation) deletes pieces of the nearest line with text below it, from its start. An `end` is one piece, `function greet(): string` goes as `string`, `:`, `)`, and so on. The indentation and trailing spaces of that line go together with the piece next to them. A line with nothing left is removed, the cursor stays on its empty line.
plua.renameClassPeek.markdownDescription: F2 on the name of a class (command `Plua: Rename Class`) renames the declaration and the `extends` of the classes that extend it. Before the new name is asked for, a peek window lists those places. Switch it off to go straight to the name.
plua.heirsPeek.markdownDescription: Select the name of a class (the whole word) and the classes that extend it (`class Human extends Entity`, and the ones that extend those, down the chain of `extends`) are shown in a peek window like the one of Peek Definition, if they are out of sight: in another file, or in this one outside of the lines on the screen. What is on the screen is not shown again, the editor marks it.
plua.heirsPeekDelayMs.markdownDescriptio: How long (in milliseconds) the selection has to stay before the window with the heirs of the selected class opens (see `plua.heirsPeek`).
plua.backspaceRemovesBlankLine.markdownD: Backspace on a line that holds nothing but spaces or tabs removes the whole line and puts the cursor at the end of the line above, instead of deleting the indentation one step at a time.
plua.shiftDeleteByPieces.markdownDescrip: Shift + Delete deletes one piece of the line per press: a word (letters, digits, `_`) or a run of one other character, with the spaces in front of it. For `self.name` with the cursor at the end the presses take `name`, `.` and `self` one after another.
plua.diagnostics.enable.markdownDescript: Show errors and warnings in the editor and the Problems panel: compiler errors (when a Pluto compiler is found, see `#plua.diagnostics.compilerPath#`) and built-in checks (missing `require` targets, calls with too few arguments, problems in `info.json`).
plua.diagnostics.compilerPath.markdownDe: Path to the Pluto compiler used to check code without running it (`plutoc`, or the `pluto` interpreter). Supports `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}` and `${env:NAME}`. When empty, a compiler inside the workspace is used (e.g. `pluto/*/plutoc.exe`, `tools/pluto/pluto.exe`, `bin/pluto`; the newest version wins), then `plutoc`/`pluto` from `PATH`. If none is found, only the built-in checks run.
plua.diagnostics.debounceMs.description: Delay in milliseconds after the last edit before a Pluto file is checked again.
command.convertLayout.title: Plua: Convert Keyboard Layout
plua.layoutFixer.enabled.markdownDescrip: Fix text typed on the wrong keyboard layout: Cyrillic keys are turned into the English keys of the same place (`дщсфд` becomes `local`). Only code is changed, not comments or strings. How it works is set by `#plua.layoutFixer.mode#`; the command `Plua: Convert Keyboard Layout` converts a selection or the current line by hand.
plua.layoutFixer.mode.markdownDescriptio: When the layout fixer converts. Keys that give a quote (`э` -> `'`, `Э` -> `"`) open a string at once in every mode except `off`; Russian text inside the string stays as it is.
plua.layoutFixer.mode.enumDescriptions.0: Every key at once, in code.
plua.layoutFixer.mode.enumDescriptions.1: A word of Cyrillic keys in code, when a space or a sign ends it.
plua.layoutFixer.mode.enumDescriptions.2: Only words that give a Pluto/Lua keyword (`local`, `function`, `end`...), when a space or a sign ends them.
plua.layoutFixer.mode.enumDescriptions.3: No automatic conversion; only the command works.
plua.layoutFixer.baseKeyboardProfile.mar: Which keys are converted. A `.` or `,` typed on the Russian layout cannot be told from an English one while typing, so signs of the Russian layout (`.` `,` `;` `:` `?` `№`) are converted only by the command, next to Cyrillic letters, and only with `physicalQwerty`.
plua.layoutFixer.baseKeyboardProfile.enu: Strict physical keys: letters, quotes, brackets, `;` `:` `,` `.` and the backtick (`х` -> `[`, `б` -> `,`, `ю` -> `.`).
Letters, quotes, brackets and `;` `:`; the keys `б` `ю` `ё` and all signs stay.
Letters and quotes only; the signs of the local layout stay as typed.
plua.layoutFixer.ignoreStrings.markdownD: Do not convert inside string literals (`"..."`, `'...'`, `[[...]]`).
plua.layoutFixer.autoCloseCyrillicQuotes: A string opened with `Э` / `э` (or any string) is closed by the same key: `Э` ends a `"` string and `э` a `'` string. In an empty string the key stays a letter, so a text may begin with `Э`.
plua.layoutFixer.customMap.markdownDescr: Your own conversions on top of the chosen profile, one character to one text, for example `{ "ё": "~" }`. An empty text keeps the character as typed.
plua.autoIndent.enabled.markdownDescript: Smart indentation on `Enter`: empty lines inside blocks keep their indentation (see `#plua.autoIndent.preserveEmptyLines#`) and the line after `case ...:` is indented by `#plua.autoIndent.indentAfterCase#`. The size of one level comes from the editor (`editor.insertSpaces`, `editor.tabSize`).
plua.autoIndent.preserveEmptyLines.markd: When `Enter` is pressed on an empty line inside a block, the line that is left and the new line get the indentation of the block, so the indent guides are not cut. Without it the editor strips the indentation of an empty line when you leave it.
plua.autoIndent.indentAfterCase.markdown: Indent the line after `case ...:` and `default:` by one level. When off, the line after a case label starts at the level of the label.
plua.autoIndent.trimOnSave.markdownDescr: Remove the whitespace of empty lines when a file is saved, to keep the file on disk clean. Only lines that hold nothing but spaces or tabs are touched.
plua.format.autoReturn.markdownDescripti: Enter after the header of a function that has a return type other than `void` (`function f(): bool`) puts a `return ` line under the empty line of the cursor, before the `end` that is added. Needs `#plua.autoCloseBlocks#`.
plua.diagnostics.returnHint.markdownDesc: When the return type of a function is taken away (`: bool` is deleted) and its body holds a `return` with a value, a grey note at the end of the header says what the function returns and what it does, and that the data type is not set. Hover it to see the code and the offer to remove the `return`; the same offer is in the quick fix (`Ctrl+.`).
plua.diagnostics.unknownTypes.markdownDe: Mark a type that is written as a type (a parameter type, a return type, `local x: Type`) and is neither a built-in type (`int`, `string`, `bool`, `table`, ...) nor a class or enum known in the workspace: `warning`, `error` or `off`.
plua.returnHelper.removeReturnWhenTypeMi: Remove a bare `return` (with no value) when the function has no usable return type: none is written, it was deleted or it is not a type (`function foo() boo`, `: boo`). Only a function whose body is nothing but that `return` is looked at, a `return` with a value is never touched, and the removal comes after a short pause. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
plua.returnHelper.moveCursorToReturnOnId: After Enter made an empty line with a `return ` below it: when the cursor rests on that empty line for `#plua.returnHelper.idleDelayMs#` and nothing is typed, the empty line goes and the cursor moves behind `return `, ready for the value.
plua.returnHelper.idleDelayMs.markdownDe: How long the cursor must rest, in milliseconds, before it moves behind the `return ` (see `#plua.returnHelper.moveCursorToReturnOnIdle#`).
The directive `#return = <expression>` written on a line of its own in the body of a function: when you press Enter or pause, the line goes and the expression becomes the `return` at the end of the function (it replaces the last `return`, or a new one is added before the `end`). One Ctrl+Z takes it back.
plua.liveDirectives.enabled.markdownDesc: Live directives: a line `#<target> = <value>` changes the value of the target (a variable, a parameter, a field such as `self.hp`, or the `return` of the function) when you press Enter, and `#<target> >show_up` / `>show_down` show what is above / below. The same lines in a comment (`-- #speed >show_up`) stay in the code and keep their grey note up to date.
plua.liveDirectives.maxPreviewLength.mar: The longest text of a grey note, in characters; a longer value is cut with `…`, the full code is in the hover.
plua.liveDirectives.maxContextLines.mark: How many lines of code the hover of a directive shows around the place that was found.
plua.liveDirectives.maxSearchDistance.ma: How many lines above / below a directive are searched for its target, so that large files stay fast.
plua.liveDirectives.completion.markdownD: Completion after `#` (the `return`, the parameters, the locals and the `self.` fields that are in reach) and after `#<target> >` (`show_up`, `show_down`).
plua.liveDirectives.inComments.markdownD: Also work on lines in a comment (`-- #speed >show_up`): they stay in the code, which still compiles.
plua.liveDirectives.allowModify.markdown: Allow the directives to change values with `=`. When off, only the commands that look (`>show_up`, `>show_down`) work and a `#name = value` line only says that changing is off.
plua.liveDirectives.skipConst.markdownDe: Do not let a directive change a variable that is a constant: `local x <const> = 1` or `const x = 1`. The grey note then says so. Turn off to change them anyway.
plua.liveDirectives.ignoredTargets.markd: Names that the directives ignore: no grey note, no change, no completion. One name per line; `*` stands for any characters (`self._*`).
plua.liveDirectives.prefix.markdownDescr: The sign that starts a directive, `#` by default (for example `@` or `$`); in a comment it follows the `--`. Up to 3 characters, no spaces. A change works at once.
plua.liveDirectives.commandSeparator.mar: The sign between the target and the command, `>` by default (for example `::` or `->`). Up to 4 characters that are not letters, digits or spaces. A change works at once.
plua.liveDirectives.commandAliases.markd: Other names for the commands: `{ "up": "show_up", "down": "show_down" }` lets you write `#speed >up`. The values are `show_up` or `show_down`; the names stay as they are.
